text_blocks.snippet: One factor that can reduce the risk of ovarian cancer is using oral contraceptives (birth control pills). Studies suggest that taking oral contraceptives for an extended period, like five years or more, can significantly lower the risk of developing ovarian cancer, according to the American Medical Association and the CDC. This is thought to be because oral contraceptives suppress ovulation, potentially reducing the number of times the ovarian surface is damaged and needs repair.

list.title: Reduced Ovulation:
list.snippet: Ovarian cancer risk is linked to the number of times a woman ovulates. Each ovulation can cause minor damage to the ovarian surface, which may lead to mutations and, potentially, cancer. Oral contraceptives prevent ovulation, thus reducing this risk factor.
